# Tests of go test's analysis driver, which replaces its use of cmd/vet
# (enabled by GOEXPERIMENT=vetfiles).

[short] skip 'builds and runs an analysis tool'
[!compiler:gc] skip

env GOEXPERIMENT=vetfiles

# The default vet checks run, via the analysis tool, not cmd/vet. As
# with cmd/vet, the test does not run if they find problems.
! go test -x ./bad
stderr 'bad.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
stdout '^FAIL\s+example.com/m/bad \[build failed\]$'
! stderr '[/\\]vet(\.exe)?"? .*vet\.cfg'

# A package with no problems passes.
go test ./good
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/m/good'

# -vet=off runs no analysis.
go test -vet=off ./bad
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/m/bad'

# -vet selects analyzers by name: printf is not among these.
go test -vet=bools,nilfunc ./bad
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/m/bad'

# -vet=all runs every analyzer of the suite, including those not in
# go test's default list (here, unusedresult).
go test ./unused
! go test -vet=all ./unused
stderr 'unused.go:5:12: result of fmt.Sprint call not used'
# Every analyzer of the vet suite passes the driver's validation.
! stderr '\(via |suite element|suite contains'

# A package without test files is analyzed too.
! go test ./notests
stderr 'notests.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
stdout '^FAIL\s+example.com/m/notests \[build failed\]$'

# printf runs on dependencies too, so it recognizes calls to printf
# wrappers declared in other packages (using facts).
! go test ./wrapcall
stderr 'wrapcall.go:5:26: example.com/m/wrapper.Logf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'

# When benchmarking, the checks run before the benchmarks (so as not to
# disturb them), which do not run if the checks fail.
! go test -run=^$ -bench=. -benchtime=1x ./bad
stdout '^FAIL\s+example.com/m/bad \[build failed\]$'
! stdout 'BenchmarkF'

# Unlike with cmd/vet, go test -c runs no checks, since it is a build.
go test -c -o=$WORK/bad.test ./bad
! stderr 'wrong type'
exists $WORK/bad.test

# With -json, the checks run before the test, which does not run if
# they fail.
! go test -json ./bad
stdout '"Action":"build-fail"'
stdout '"Action":"fail","Package":"example.com/m/bad",.*"FailedBuild":"example.com/m/bad \[example.com/m/bad.test\]"'
! stdout '"Test":"TestF"'

# The tool is built in this process, in the tests' build configuration,
# whatever their build flags: here, -tags, -cover (whose generated
# files are in the build directory), and -race.
! go test -x -tags=x ./bad
stderr 'analysistool(\.exe)?"? .*analysis\.cfg'
stderr 'bad.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
! go test -cover ./bad
stderr 'bad.go:5:\d+: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
[race] ! go test -race ./bad
[race] stderr 'bad.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'

# A type error (here, because -gcflags overrides the language version
# for the compiler but not for analysis) is reported once, not once
# per analyzer.
cd old
! go test -gcflags=-lang=go1.26 .
stderr -count=1 'new\(1\) requires go1\.26 or later'
cd ..

# Under an exec wrapper, which may run the tests in an emulator or a
# sandbox, go test does not run the tool on the host: it uses cmd/vet.
! go test -x -exec=echo ./bad
stderr '[/\\]vet(\.exe)?"? .*vet\.cfg'
! stderr 'analysistool'
stderr 'bad.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'

# The tool is built for the tests' platform and runs on the host, so
# when the tests are cross-compiled without an exec wrapper, it cannot
# run (nor can the tests).
[GOOS:linux] env GOOS=windows
[!GOOS:linux] env GOOS=linux
env GOARCH=amd64 # a valid pair with either GOOS, whatever the host's GOARCH
! go test ./good
stderr '^running analysis tool built for (linux|windows)/amd64: '
stderr '^\(to run the tests on another platform, use -exec; to disable analysis, use -vet=off\)$'

# With an exec wrapper, cross-compiled tests are checked by cmd/vet.
! go test -exec=echo ./bad
stderr 'bad.go:5:39: fmt.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
env GOOS=
env GOARCH=

# go test -n shows the tool's metadata query and, for each root
# package, a placeholder for its analysis (which cannot be planned
# without the metadata).
go test -n ./good
stderr 'analysistool(\.exe)?"? "?-describe='
stderr 'analysistool(\.exe)? \$WORK[/\\]b\d+[/\\]analysis\.cfg # analyzers determined by -describe$'

# -vet accepts the legacy analyzer names that cmd/vet accepts.
go test -vet=bool,buildtags,methods,rangeloops ./good

# Analysis handles cgo packages, whose generated files live in the cgo objdir.
[cgo] ! go test ./cgobad
[cgo] stderr 'cgobad\.go:8:.*fmt\.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
[cgo] ! go test -cover ./cgobad
[cgo] stderr 'cgobad\.go:8:.*fmt\.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'

# The positions of diagnostics are those of overlay files, even if
# overlays of the same content at different paths were analyzed before.
! go test -overlay=ov1.json ./good
stderr 'o1[/\\]good\.go:5:39: fmt\.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'
! go test -overlay=ov2.json ./good
stderr 'o2[/\\]good\.go:5:39: fmt\.Sprintf format %d has arg "x" of wrong type string'

-- ov1.json --
{"Replace":{"good/good.go":"o1/good.go"}}
-- ov2.json --
{"Replace":{"good/good.go":"o2/good.go"}}
-- o1/good.go --
package good

import "fmt"

func F() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d", "x") }
-- o2/good.go --
package good

import "fmt"

func F() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d", "x") }
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.28
-- bad/bad.go --
package bad

import "fmt"

func F() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d", "x") }
-- bad/bad_test.go --
package bad

import "testing"

func TestF(t *testing.T) { F() }

func BenchmarkF(b *testing.B) {
	for b.Loop() {
		F()
	}
}
-- notests/notests.go --
package notests

import "fmt"

func F() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d", "x") }
-- good/good.go --
package good

func F() int { return 1 }
-- good/good_test.go --
package good

import "testing"

func TestF(t *testing.T) { F() }
-- old/go.mod --
module example.com/old

go 1.21
-- old/old.go --
package old

func F() *int { return new(1) }
-- old/old_test.go --
package old
-- unused/unused.go --
package unused

import "fmt"

func F() { fmt.Sprint("x") }
-- unused/unused_test.go --
package unused

import "testing"

func TestF(t *testing.T) { F() }
-- cgobad/cgobad.go --
package cgobad

import "C"
import "fmt"

func F() string {
	var _ C.int
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d", "x")
}
-- cgobad/cgobad_test.go --
package cgobad

import "testing"

func TestF(t *testing.T) { F() }
-- wrapper/wrapper.go --
package wrapper

import "fmt"

func Logf(format string, args ...any) { fmt.Printf(format, args...) }
-- wrapcall/wrapcall.go --
package wrapcall

import "example.com/m/wrapper"

func F() { wrapper.Logf("%d", "x") }
